name: fetchHtml() does not retry at all
why: The pre-F1 behaviour: one attempt, and a single 503 on page 2 ends the run at page 1. The recovery test must notice both the missing retry and the missing rows.

name: every status is retried, 4xx included
why: The overshoot rather than the defect. Widening a retry set is exactly the change that goes too far, and without the boundary test a page fetch would spend three attempts on every 404 on the site.

name: Retry-After is ignored on the HTML path
why: The header half. 503 is retried either way, so only the WAIT changes: the retry lands at the bare 2000 ms backoff instead of the 5000 ms the server asked for.
grep: honoured as a floor on the page backoff

name: the failed page is counted as loaded again
why: F1 itself, reproduced by putting the increment back on the failure path: `pagesProcessed` then includes the page that 503'd and the line reads "2 of 3". Note the test asserts the NUMBER, not merely that a warning appeared — a warning would still be there.

edits.find:
fetchIncomplete.pageFailure = { page: p, detail: _httpFailureDetail(e) };
                    break; // Stop fetching further pages on error

name: a failed page is logged but not recorded
why: The other half of F1: without the record every reporting surface goes back to describing a truncated run in the words of a complete one.

name: fetchMaxPageGeneric() reports a failed count as OK
why: F2 restored: `maxPage` is still 1, so the run looks like a complete one-page listing — which is exactly how this survived, since the old JSDoc documented it as intended.

name: an unknown page count prints "N of M" anyway
why: M is the fallback 1 when the count could not be read, so this makes the line read "Loaded 1 of 1 pages" — a complete one-page listing, the same lie in new words. This is the whole reason pagesPhrase distinguishes the two cases.

edits.find:
const pagesPhrase = rec.pageFailure
            ? `${pagesProcessed} of ${maxPage} pages`
            : (rec.maxPageUnknown
                ? `${pagesProcessed} ${plural} of an unknown total`
                : `${pagesProcessed} ${plural}`);

name: a short official set is handed on instead of discarded
why: F3: the partial set survives, so the view buttons are built from it and the walk misfiles genuinely-official categories as non-official. Discarding is also what stops `discOfficialCategories` persisting the wrong split to disk.

name: an incomplete pre-fetch is not recorded
why: Without the record nothing discards the partial set and nothing tells the user why the discography buttons are missing — the run looks entirely clean.

name: a pre-fetch failure marks the ROWS incomplete
why: The severity distinction. The main pass is independent of the pre-fetch, so its rows really are all there; calling that set INCOMPLETE would train the user to ignore the word, which is the only thing making it useful.
